reason: The passage (Song of the Sea, Exodus 15) distinguishes between the Israelites and their Egyptian enemies, but this distinction is based on God's power, divine choice, and redemptive action—not on any claim of inherent superiority. The text emphasizes that the Israelites are 'a people whom you have redeemed' (קָנִֽיתָ), highlighting God's covenant choice rather than natural excellence. Similarly, the destruction of Egypt's elite (Pharaoh's chariots and chosen warriors) is attributed entirely to God's might ('Your right hand, O Lord, shatters the enemy'), not to any inherent superiority of the Israelites as a people. The passage celebrates divine power, not human hierarchies based on inherent worth.
